title: midnight-scrap-handoff-sr-serve-candidate-kai-garcia
body:
Quick context: loop finished today (onsite-lite: design + pairing + behavioral). Candidate: Kai Garcia. Role: Senior Serving Reliability / Inference Platform. My notes are messy — will hand off to Maya for formal write-up, but leaving raw impressions and leveling rationale here (overnight gut-check).

First impressions / vibe:
- Calm, deliberate communicator; asks clarifying questions before diving in (good).
- Comfortable drawing system diagrams on the whiteboard; used precise latency/cost tradeoff language.
- Some small jokes — humanized the room without derailing.

Technical highlights seen in loop:
- Design exercise: proposed a multi-tier fallback routing for model variants (baseline -> quantized -> smaller model) with weight decay-based circuit-breaker. Good awareness of degradation modes and how to instrument SLOs.
- Pairing task: implemented a simplified KV-cache eviction policy for a mocked transformer KV store; code was readable, tested edge cases, but used a library helper where I expected a short custom comparator. Not a blocker but indicates pragmatic leaning.
- Behavioral: described prior ownership of autoscaler tuning for a mixed-GPU fleet; cited concrete metrics (reduced p99 by ~18% after tuning burst policies) — numbers felt plausible and specific.

Risks / unknowns:
- No deep CUDA/kernel-level talk; when pressed about memory-bound vs compute-bound inference bottlenecks, answer was at a high level (batching + quant). For a role that may need kernel debugging, this is moderate risk.
- Security/compliance experience limited: mentioned working with VPCs and KMS in previous role but hasn't owned SOC2 artifacts. For Dedicated/Private work this might need pairing with PMs.
- Distributed debugging: good conceptual approach but limited examples of cross-region failure postmortems they personally led.

Strengths:
- Systems-level thinking for serving tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs reliability).
- Shipping mentality — pragmatic choices, tends to favor measurable wins.
- Clear collaborator; would integrate well with SRE and infra PMs.

Weaknesses / development areas:
- Lower depth on low-level (CUDA/FP16 kernels) and infra security artifacts ownership.
- Could improve on proactively surfacing long-term design debt; tends to optimize for near-term measurable wins.

Suggested leveling & hire stance:
- Level: Senior (IC4) seems appropriate. Could be considered IC5 if paired with a strong kernel/quant engineer for low-level bits, but not today.
- Recommendation: strong hire if we need a pragmatic serving owner who can scope rollouts and reduce unit cost quickly. Consider hiring contingent on pairing interview focused on low-level perf and a short take-home to exercise kernel/quant reasoning (not necessarily CUDA coding, but quantitative tradeoffs with microbenchmarks).

Calibration notes for panel handoff:
- Flag to interviewers: push for a concrete walk-through of a past incident they owned (timeline, mitigations, postmortem outcomes). We want to see explicit actions they took and what changed.
- Ask Security: bring up KMS/VPC ownership and what artifacts they maintained, who they coordinated with, and how they validated controls.
- Perf deep-dive: ask for specific microbenchmarking framework they've used and an example where they had to choose an algorithm/kernel change vs infra change.

Suggested next steps (practical):
1) Short async follow-up question for candidate: "Describe a single production incident where latency p99 regressed. What were the top 3 hypotheses you tested and how did you prioritize fixes?" — aim to get concrete commands/metrics.
2) If answer satisfies, run a focused 60m kernel/perf interview with one of our runtime engineers (Marcus or Aya).
3) Draft offer if that goes well; recommend IC4 comp band.

Notes-to-self (things to include in formal debrief):
- Capture exact numbers Kai cited during autoscaler tuning (ask for artifact links).
- Confirm familiarity with our observability stack (OTel + Datadog) — they mentioned Prometheus but not OTel.
- Determine willingness/comfort to pair with a kernel engineer on low-level perf improvements (mentorship style).

Raw scoring (quick):
- Technical breadth: 4/5
- Low-level depth: 2.5/5
- Communication: 5/5
- Ownership/Incidents: 3.5/5
- Overall hire likelihood: 80% (lean hire)

Random scribbles to include in handoff doc:
- "likes measurable impact"
- "asks clarifying Qs first"
- "pragmatic — used helper libs in pairing"
- "needs kernel perf stretch"

End of notes — will clean into formal debrief doc tomorrow. If Maya wants me to write a short candidate blurb for hiring committee, I can convert this into a 5-sentence summary.

-- Devon
